english: Consider the ellipse $E:\dfrac{x^{2}}{6}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{3}=1$ and the hyperbola $H:\dfrac{x^{2}}{5}-y^{2}=1$. A line $L$ is a tangent to $E$ and is also the normal to $H$ at a point $Q$ of $H$ lying in the second quadrant. Then the $x$-coordinate of $Q$ is ______.
hindi: दीर्घवृत्त $E:\dfrac{x^{2}}{6}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{3}=1$ तथा अतिपरवलय $H:\dfrac{x^{2}}{5}-y^{2}=1$ पर विचार कीजिए। एक रेखा $L$, $E$ की स्पर्श रेखा है और द्वितीय चतुर्थांश में स्थित $H$ के एक बिन्दु $Q$ पर $H$ का अभिलम्ब भी है। तब $Q$ का $x$-निर्देशांक ______ है।
solution: Normal to $H$ at $Q(x_{1},y_{1})$: $\dfrac{5x}{x_{1}}+\dfrac{y}{y_{1}}=6$. Write it as $lx+ny=1$ with $l=\dfrac{5}{6x_{1}}$, $n=\dfrac{1}{6y_{1}}$
solution_full: Let $Q(x_{1},y_{1})$ lie on $H$, so $\dfrac{x_{1}^{2}}{5}-y_{1}^{2}=1$ with $x_{1}<0<y_{1}$. The tangent at $Q$ is $\dfrac{xx_{1}}{5}-yy_{1}=1$, and the normal is $\dfrac{a^{2}x}{x_{1}}+\dfrac{b^{2}y}{y_{1}}=a^{2}+b^{2}$, i.e. $\dfrac{5x}{x_{1}}+\dfrac{y}{y_{1}}=6$.
The line $lx+ny=1$ touches $\dfrac{x^{2}}{6}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{3}=1$ if and only if $6l^{2}+3n^{2}=1$ (the condition $a^{2}l^{2}+b^{2}n^{2}=1$ for a tangent to an ellipse).
$X=\dfrac{115\pm\sqrt{13225-12000}}{24}=\dfrac{115\pm35}{24}$, so $X=\dfrac{25}{4}$ or $X=\dfrac{10}{3}$. Since $x_{1}^{2}\ge5$ on $H$, only $X=\dfrac{25}{4}$ is admissible.
Then $y_{1}^{2}=\dfrac{25/4-5}{5}=\dfrac14$. With $Q$ in the second quadrant, $Q=\left(-\dfrac52,\dfrac12\right)$.
Check: the normal at $Q$ is $\dfrac{5x}{-5/2}+\dfrac{y}{1/2}=6$, i.e. $y=x+3$; for $E$, $c^{2}=9=6\cdot1^{2}+3=a^{2}m^{2}+b^{2}$, so it is a tangent.
originality_note: New: the same line plays two roles, tangent to an ellipse and normal to a hyperbola, and the foot of the normal is recovered through the line-coordinate tangency condition (way 5). Closest known: common tangents of an ellipse and a hyperbola; normals of a hyperbola through a point. Different because: a tangent of one conic is matched with a normal of the other, and a spurious root X = 10/3 must be rejected because it gives no point of H.

concept_use.Tangent and normal for Hyperbola: The normal to H at Q(x1, y1), 5x/x1 + y/y1 = 6, supplies the line whose coefficients are tested; Q in the second quadrant fixes the sign of x1.
concept_use.Tangent and normal for Ellipse: The tangency condition a^2 l^2 + b^2 n^2 = 1 for the ellipse E gives the equation 12X^2 - 115X + 250 = 0 for X = x1^2.

stem_review: Read as a student: every curve, point and symbol is introduced, the conditions are complete, each sentence has one reading; answer recomputed with sympy and unique; it matches the Answer Plan. Checked that the extraneous root X = 10/3 gives no point of H, that the second-quadrant condition makes Q unique, and that -2.5 is exact. Changed: No change.
key_step: Writing the normal of H in line coordinates and imposing the ellipse tangency condition, then rejecting the root with y1^2 < 0.
justification: Two ideas linked (normal of a hyperbola, tangency condition of an ellipse) with a root to reject, in numerical form. Comparable to 2023-P1-Q2 (L3); harder than the routine tangent chain of 2026-P2-Q17 (L2).
